patch.objective: Protect client self-determination and the right to refuse services, and recognize when imminent risk limits it
secondaryObjectives: Assess a client's capacity for decisions about money, treatment and consent, including emancipation and age of consent

sources.cite: NASW Code of Ethics (2021 revision): 1.02 self-determination, limited when clients' actions 'pose a serious, foreseeable, and imminent risk to themselves or others'; 1.03(c)-(d); 1.07(c) minimum necessary; 1.07(d) notice before disclosure; 1.07(j) court orders: ask the court to withdraw or limit the order or keep records under seal; 1.14; 1.17(a)-(b)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on socialworkers.org (summarizing fetch with short quotes; the page shows the 2021 code). Amendments were to be voted 2026-11-18; recheck by 2026-12-15.

sources.cite: Appelbaum PS. Assessment of patients' competence to consent to treatment. N Engl J Med 2007;357(18):1834-1840, as summarized by the AMA Journal of Ethics (August 2008): four abilities: expressing a choice, understanding the relevant information, appreciating the consequences for oneself, and reasoning about the options
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in the AMA Journal of Ethics summary (summarizing fetch); the NEJM article itself was not opened.

sources.cite: RCW 71.05.153(1) (2023 c 433 s 9): a designated crisis responder may take a person into emergency custody when, 'as the result of a behavioral health disorder', the person presents an 'imminent likelihood of serious harm' or is in 'imminent danger because of being gravely disabled'
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on the Legislature's page for the section (summarizing fetch with short quotes). It is not a tool for overriding a capable person's refusal of medical treatment.

brief.situation: You are a licensed social worker in a Washington hospital emergency department. Earl Thompson, 58 (a fictional patient), has diabetes and an infected ulcer on his left foot. The physician has recommended admission tonight for IV antibiotics and has explained the risks of leaving: the infection could spread, he could lose the foot, and it could become life-threatening. Earl says he is going home. The nurse pages you: 'Can you talk him into staying, or get him held?' You have about 45 minutes.
